title: An integral algebra over a henselian pair gives a henselian pair
statement: Let $(A,I)$ be a henselian pair [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology] and let $A\to B$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings with $B$ integral over $A$ (every element of $B$ is a root of a monic polynomial with coefficients in the image of $A$). Then $(B,IB)$ is a henselian pair: for every finite $B$-algebra $C$, every idempotent of $C/IC$ lifts uniquely to an idempotent of $C$.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma 15.11.8 (Tag 09XK, label lemma-integral-over-henselian-pair, line 2753), using the characterization (4) of Lemma 15.11.6 (Tag 09XI, lemma-characterize-henselian-pair: idempotent lifting for integral algebras)

proof.text: Put J = I.map (algebraMap A B). The extended ideal J lies in the Jacobson radical of B: the contraction of each maximal ideal M of an integral A-algebra is maximal [lem-weil-pbc-integral-maximal-contracts-maximal], using Mathlib Ideal.isMaximal_comap_of_isIntegral_of_isMaximal, hence contains I by HenselianRing.jac. Ideal.map_le_iff_le_comap gives J <= M. Intersect over M.

For a monic f in B[X], let C = AdjoinRoot f, a finite B-algebra. It is integral over B by finite-implies-integral, and integral over A by Algebra.IsIntegral.trans B for the composite algebra structure. Ideal.map_map identifies J.map (algebraMap B C) with I.map (algebraMap A C). Apply Algebra.existsUnique_isIdempotentElem_of_henselianRing A I C to lift each idempotent in this quotient.

For a coprime monic factorization f mod J = g0*h0, Bezout coefficients a*g0+b*h0=1 give the idempotent b*h0 in C/JC. Lift it by the preceding step. Quotient maps into AdjoinRoot g0 and AdjoinRoot h0 send the lift to 1 and 0, respectively: their kernels contain JC and the Bezout identity computes the residues. Polynomial.exists_monic_factorization_of_idempotent supplies the monic factors of f lifting g0 and h0. This argument is inlined in henselianRing_of_isIntegral; it follows the Bezout calculation of Tag 09XI (3) implies (1), also used by the inaccessible private helper factorization_of_lifting in HenselianFactorizationCriterion.

Apply the reverse implication of henselianRing_iff_factorization_criterion B J to the Jacobson condition from step 1 and the factorization lifting from step 3. This yields HenselianRing B J in Mathlib's simple-root formulation. No unit-level step is bypassed.
